defect.summary: A GRANT WIDENED LATER RE-LABELS AN OLD DAMAGE RECORD (S216; Long Run A Stop 2 F-2; canon M3): the served reader (2511dac, index.ts:1878) reads the CURRENT grant for every record whenever it was written, so a declaration that widens an item's grant to the origin ends a standing latch without the doctor's clearance — and a restart, which H11 cannot refuse, lays such a declaration. Canon M3: a latch clears only by a clearance.
defect.ground: Board 2026-10-16 05:20Z ('S216 REGISTERED, owed before publication: grants carry a `since`, only a clearance ends a latch'); T31's signature (F-2: 'S216 … is owed before publication'); the draft ARC_MICA-TICKET_S216-Grant-Since_DRAFT_20261016.md; the night dispatch 2026-10-16 19:1xZ (S216 on the line as DRAFT tickets for signature on 2511dac / 248b277). MECHANISM: config.harm gains `grantSince` (item -> origin -> {at: ms, utc}), exactly the keys of `grants`, refused whole otherwise (G2_HARM_MALFORMED — so a machine and a bridge of different S216-ness read WIRED AND BLIND, never a silent grant); granted(r) = origin listed ∧ r.timestamp is a finite number ∧ r.timestamp ≥ since.at; a listed origin's record earlier than its since is damage, printed 'NONE (o is granted I only since <utc>; this record is earlier)'; the GRANTED line names its since; the latch-exits text says a widening with a later since never ends a latch; one new harm ceiling line (18).

arbiter.word: Granted by the audit under Frank's standing delegation, 2026-10-17, on Frank's registration of S216 (2026-10-16 05:20Z) and the rulings of 2026-10-17 11:22Z: every grant counts from its since; a listed origin's record earlier than its since is damage; a widening with a later since never ends a latch; laundering closed by the window-start rule; one new harm ceiling line; the class moves to the predicted @a1595284…, voiding every unarmed sealed case (re-seal, never edit). Conditions of this signature: base is the served VINTAGE ebbdbca (relay 1 landed 2026-10-17 15:28Z), so the re-pins run from relay 1's blobs and T36's live arm is amended in this commit (cond. 8; the live-arc data file is in the opens); cond. 7 is reworded as ruled and the restart exit is printed, not hidden, until S216-2; the bridge half (s216-grant-since-bridge, with the S198 copy-back of S36) relays as ONE act after this machine relay and after gate2-2's SCORED line (on the register since 2026-10-17 15:3xZ); AA4's amendment M1.4a (grantSince in U3's hand-built config) rides this commit; glue.test.ts's edit is covered by T33's document (A-2). expiresAt 2026-10-24T18:00:00Z is the audit's fill and part of this signature.

The relay order is the bridge's tree declaration and code as ONE act after the machine, and NOT before gate2-2's SCORED line (or gate2-2 is re-sealed): S216 moves the harm class (G2_HARM_V2; served @e8b6390a… → predicted @a1595284d927ca02), which voids every unarmed case (the register's header rule, 2026-10-16 18:2xZ).

A record AT its since is granted; one ms before is not (≥, killed mutant ge-as-gt); a record with no usable timestamp is never granted (killed mutant no-timestamp-granted); since ignored → killed (since-ignored); a granted origin with no since accepted → killed (since-missing-accepted). The REFUTER M3 'grant widened' arm FLIPS: widened with a since after the record → ALARM; back-dated to the record → not ALARM, the restart path a reload refuses (H11 c').

THE NO-TIMESTAMP FENCE IS AMENDED NARROWLY, still biting: outside the harm markers word for word; inside, the instant reads are pinned as FOUR (a book's first line, the witness record's own timestamp — new — and a roster entry snapshotted, compared); no Date anywhere in the reader (the since's UTC spelling arrives injected and is printed as given). The calibration fence is unchanged (no new number).

REMOVAL REHEARSAL (g2b-notes/s216/rehearsal/removal.ts, 3000 random fixture books on subject-r / r-1..r-3 / o-r, seed 20261016): (a) every since before every record → 3000 of 3000 identical to the 2511dac reader in kind, code, latchedSince and harmLine minus ' since …'; (b) random since → no 2511dac ALARM is lost (892 ALARMs kept), and 349 readings newly ALARM where a grant did not yet count. 5. NO SERVED LITERAL in the reader or its ceilings; the tests' only box-derived values are T36's fixture (ids renamed, every other value live), by T36's own ruling (fixtures: 'fixture-since', u-at, U<ms>).

WHAT THIS TICKET DOES NOT FIX: the record's timestamp is the book's own (the witness's clock); a witness clock that lies moves whether a record is granted (printed in the new ceiling line); a restart may still lay a back-dated since (H11 refuses it on reload only; the harmClass on every verdict shows the stanza read); errand-level origin is still S208-2.

RULED (audit 2026-10-17 11:22Z, on Frank's ruling of 2026-10-16 05:20Z — the WHAT is not a fork): 'only a clearance ends a latch' is delivered for every grant written honestly — a widening with a LATER since never ends a latch, and laundering (a change first seen after the since but made before it) reads ungranted. The one exit left is a since BACK-DATED ACROSS A RESTART (H11 refuses it on reload only); it reaches the stateless reader byte-identical to an honest grant, so it is S216-2's (a durable grant memory in /var/lib/mica-bridge, effective since = max(declared, first-seen), seeded by Frank at relay; its own ticket after T34). Until S216-2 lands the ALARM text prints that exit as a ceiling: 'a restart is a first load: a declaration back-dating a grant across it is not refused today'. The other exits that end or blind a latch without a clearance (item removal, origin removal or re-binding, a moved book across a restart, salt-epoch loss, a predecessor-only latch whose book becomes unreadable) stay named in the ALARM's exits text, each as what it is.
